Read and adhere to all warnings, cautions, and notices in this guide and the
documentation supplied with the chassis, power supply, and accessory modules. If
the instructions for the chassis and power supply are inconsistent with these
instructions or the instructions for accessory modules, contact the supplier to find out
how you can ensure that your device meets safety and regulatory requirements.
Electrostatic discharge (ESD) can damage system components. Do the described
procedures only at an ESD workstation. If no such station is available, you can
provide some ESD protection by wearing an antistatic wrist strap and attaching it to a
metal part of the computer chassis.
1. Read these safety instructions carefully.
2. Keep this User Manual for later reference.
3. Disconnect this equipment from any AC outlet before cleaning. Use a damp
cloth. Do not use liquid or spray detergents for cleaning.
4. For plug-in equipment, the power outlet socket must be located near the
equipment and must be easily accessible.
5. Keep this equipment away from humidity.
6. Put this equipment on a stable surface during installation. Dropping it or letting
7. Make sure the voltage of the power source is correct before connecting the
equipment to the power outlet.
8. Place the power cord in a way so that people will not step on it. Do not place
anything on top of the power cord. Use a power cord that has been approved
for use with the product and that it matches the voltage and current marked
on the product’s electrical range label. The voltage and current rating of the
cord must be greater than the voltage and current rating marked on the
9. All cautions and warnings on the equipment should be noted.
10.If the equipment is not used for a long time, disconnect it from the power
source to avoid damage by transient overvoltage.
11.Never pour any liquid into an opening. This may cause fire or electrical shock.
12.Never open the equipment. For safety reasons, the equipment should be
opened only by qualified service personnel.
13.If one of the following situations arises, get the equipment checked by service
a. The power cord or plug is damaged.
b. Liquid has penetrated into the equipment.
c. The equipment has been exposed to moisture.
d. The equipment does not work well, or you cannot get it to work
according to the user’s manual.
e. The equipment has been dropped and damaged.
f. The equipment has obvious signs of breakage.
14.Do not place heavy objects on the equipment.

CloudPlug light is based on a microcontroller system that has 8 inputs (configurable as
digital or analog inputs) and a serial RS485 (Modbus) interface to collect user data.
The data is transmitted via the integrated LTE module (Quectel BG96) to Google IoT Core.
The device for collecting user data is configured via Google IoT Core.
Before using the CloudPlug light an external GSM antenna has to be connected.
There may occur interference on data transmission during burst pulses on supply line, that
could lead CloudPlug light to do automatic reboot and reconnect to Google IoT Core.
Depending on the signal quality of mobile network there may also occur connection aborts
User data will be stored on the device and transmitted automatically after a connection
successfully established again.
CloudPlug light can be connected to a PC via the integrated USB interface. The device
appears as a virtual COM port on the PC. (suitable driver required)

5. Right-Click on Cloudplug Light USB Device 0 and install the driver manually
6. After successful installation of the driver Windows device manager shows Cloudplug

Developed by SOTEC, CloudPlug Edge is an IIoT edge hardware, designed and engineered for
industrial applications. It is capable to gather data from various machines, ranging from
manufacturing, energy, supply, infrastructure up to home automation. CloudPlug Edge achieves
this by communicating with central machine control systems like PLCs, motion control units,
HVACs a.s.o. via available interfaces and automation protocols. It supports ethernet-based
communication, RS485, CAN and digital/analog inputs.
Therea�er, data from the machine or process network can be collected, pre-processed, and stored
in a secure Cloud environment for analysis. Thanks to its small size and robust case built for
industrial use it can be deployed on DIN Rails or close to the machine. Our engineers put special
focus on a safe, modular, robust, and yet economically built. We use standard components such
as ARM processors, which can be easily adjusted for individual demands. Via the Sotec so�ware
stack, CloudPlug Edge is also capable to act as an edge device.
The CloudPlug Edge is based on a iMX7 SOM system. It has 8 inputs (configurable as digital or
analog inputs), a serial RS485 (Modbus) interface, a High speed CAN interface and two 100/1000
Mbps Ethernet interfaces to collect user data.
The data can be transmitted to Google IoT Core or a https endpoint via LAN / WLAN or optionally
via the integrated LTE module (Quectel BG96).
The setup for collecting data is configured via a local web UI.
While using LTE, depending on the signal quality of the mobile network there may also occur
connection aborts with subsequent reconnection.
On connection loss user data will be stored on the device and transmitted automatically a�er a
connection successfully established again.

12.3 Password storage, Encryption and Transport Layer Security
TheCloudPlug Edgeis delivered with standard passwordsboth for system access over ssh as well
as for access to the configuration web UI. Those standard passwords are set during factory
installation, but they are not hard coded into the source code of the system.
We highly recommend that you change these passwords during installation and apply your
own company password policy to it.
Currently there is no encryption at rest of passwords and other credentials used in the system.
Passwords for SSH users are stored hashed in a standard linux way in /etc/shadow file. Passwords
for WEB UI are stored in plain text.

The Domain Name System (DNS) is one of the most important services in IP based networks. Its
main task is to resolve host names to IP addresses. If CloudPlug Edge is not able to reach any of the
configured DNS servers it cannot resolve host names such as for the cloud portal, NTP server or
upgrade server and thus will not work properly.
Checking if DNS works properly can be done using nslookup:
If DNS port 53 UDP is blocked, you will see an error message like the following:
nslookup: can't resolve 'google.com'
If DNS works properly, the command shows the following or similar output:
Checking if DNS works properly can be done using the following ping command which only
succeeds if ping is able to resolve the host name “google.com”:
If DNS works properly, the command shows the following or similar output:
PING google.com (172.217.16.142): 56 data bytes
64 bytes from 172.217.16.142: seq=0 ttl=118 time=18.417 ms
64 bytes from 172.217.16.142: seq=1 ttl=118 time=17.603 ms
The Network Time Protocol (NTP) is used for synchronization of the CloudPlug Edgeʼs system time
with other computers in the network. This can either be a local NTP server or a globally available
In any case the protocol uses UDP port 53 for connection, so this port must be opened in the
For verification, you can use the following command:
echo "test" > /dev/udp/8.8.8.8/123
This tries to open a UDP connection to IP address 8.8.8.8 on port 123 (Google time server). If
successful, the command will just get back without any message. Otherwise, an error message is
shown similar to the following:
-sh: echo: write error: Operation not permitted
